permira::Zendesk.notes: Zendesk was acquired by an investor group led by Permira and Hellman & Friedman in November 2022 for approximately $10.2 billion. It is currently a private portfolio company of Permira.

permira::Mimecast.notes: Mimecast is a cybersecurity firm that was acquired by Permira in May 2022 for approximately $5.8 billion, taking the company private. It remains a current portfolio company of Permira as of early 2026.

permira::Neuraxpharm.notes: Neuraxpharm is a pharmaceutical company specializing in central nervous system (CNS) disorders, headquartered in Barcelona, Spain. It was acquired by Permira from Apax Partners in 2020. As of early 2026, Permira has initiated a sale process for the company, but it remains a current portfolio holding until the transaction is finalized.

permira::Adevinta.notes: Adevinta is a global online classifieds company headquartered in Oslo, Norway. It was taken private in 2024 by a consortium led by Permira and Blackstone and remains a current portfolio company as of early 2025.

permira::McAfee.notes: McAfee was taken private in March 2022 for $14 billion by an investor group led by Advent International and Permira. It remains a current portfolio company of Permira as of February 2026, with Permira Senior Advisor Bruce Chizen serving as Chairman of the Board.

permira::Dr. Martens.notes: Dr. Martens was acquired by Permira in 2014. While the company went public (IPO) on the London Stock Exchange in January 2021—an event often categorized as an 'exit' in private equity—Permira remains the largest shareholder, holding approximately 38% of the shares as of early 2026. Therefore, it is still an active portfolio company.

permira::TeamViewer.notes: TeamViewer is a real technology company headquartered in Göppingen, Germany. Permira acquired it in 2014, took it public in 2019, and completed its final exit by selling its remaining shares in September 2025.

permira::Allegro.notes: Allegro is a major Polish e-commerce platform headquartered in Poznan. Permira, alongside Cinven and Mid Europa Partners, acquired the company in 2016. While Allegro went public (IPO) on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in October 2020 and Permira has since reduced its stake through several block trades (most recently in December 2025), Permira still holds approximately 12.44% of the shares as of February 2026. Therefore, the investment is currently a 'partial exit' rather than a full exit.

permira::Klarna.notes: Klarna is a Swedish fintech company. Permira acquired a strategic equity stake (approx. 10-13%) in 2017. While Permira sold about 55% of its holding in 2021, it retained a significant minority stake. Klarna went public on the NYSE (ticker: KLAR) in September 2025, but Permira remains a shareholder as of early 2026.

permira::Reformation.notes: Reformation is a Los Angeles-based sustainable fashion brand. Permira acquired a majority stake in the company in July 2019. As of mid-2024, the company was reported to be still held by Permira with no immediate plans for an exit, and no sale or IPO has been announced as of February 2026.

permira::Avaloq.notes: Avaloq was a portfolio company of Warburg Pincus, not Permira. Warburg Pincus acquired a stake in 2017 and exited in December 2020 when Avaloq was acquired by NEC Corporation for approximately $2.2 billion. Permira was reported as a bidder in the 2020 sale process but did not win. BlackRock subsequently took a minority stake in 2023.

permira::Ancestry.com.notes: Ancestry.com was acquired by Permira in 2012. In 2016, Silver Lake and GIC acquired a majority stake, but Permira retained a minority interest. Permira fully exited its investment in December 2020 when Blackstone acquired the company for $4.7 billion. The company is headquartered in Lehi, Utah.

permira::Engel & Völkers.notes: Permira acquired a 60% majority stake in Engel & Völkers in late 2021. The company is a real estate brokerage headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, and remains a current portfolio company of Permira as of early 2025.

permira::Acne Studios.notes: Acne Studios is a real Swedish fashion house, but it is not a portfolio company of Permira. Its majority owners are founders Jonny Johansson and Mikael Schiller, with minority stakes held by IDG Capital and I.T Group since 2018. Permira has invested in other fashion brands like Golden Goose and Reformation, but not Acne Studios.

permira::Gainsight.notes: Gainsight is a real technology company headquartered in San Francisco, but it is a portfolio company of Vista Equity Partners, which acquired a majority stake in November 2020 for $1.1 billion. There is no evidence that Permira currently holds or has recently held Gainsight in its portfolio.

permira::Genesys.notes: Genesys is a customer experience software company headquartered in Daly City, USA. Permira acquired the company from Alcatel-Lucent in 2012. As of late 2025, Permira remains a majority owner alongside Hellman & Friedman, following several recapitalizations and investments from firms like Salesforce and ServiceNow.

permira::Informatica.notes: Informatica is a real technology company headquartered in Redwood City. While it was a portfolio company of Permira (acquired in 2015 and taken public in 2021), Salesforce completed its acquisition of Informatica in November 2025 for approximately $8 billion, resulting in a full exit for Permira.

permira::Cambrex.notes: Cambrex is a leading CDMO headquartered in East Rutherford, NJ. It was acquired by Permira in December 2019 for approximately $2.4 billion. As of February 2026, it remains a portfolio company of Permira, although reports in late 2025 indicated that Permira had initiated a sale process targeting a $4 billion valuation.

permira::Quotient Sciences.notes: Quotient Sciences is a Nottingham-based drug development and manufacturing accelerator. Permira acquired a majority stake in the company in July 2019 from GHO Capital and remains the primary owner as of early 2026.

permira::I-MED Radiology Network.notes: I-MED Radiology Network is a major diagnostic imaging provider headquartered in Sydney, Australia. It was acquired by Permira in January 2018 from EQT Partners. As of February 2026, it remains a portfolio company of Permira; although Permira attempted to sell the business in 2024 and 2025 (with a deal with Stonepeak reportedly falling through in June 2025), no exit has been finalized, and the company is currently considered a held asset.

permira::Exclusive Networks.notes: Exclusive Networks is a cybersecurity specialist based in Boulogne-Billancourt, France. Permira acquired a majority stake in 2018 and remained a major shareholder after its 2021 IPO. In early 2025, a consortium led by Permira and CD&R completed a take-private acquisition, delisting the company from Euronext Paris. It is currently held by Permira and CD&R.

permira::Lytx.notes: Lytx is a San Diego-based technology company specializing in video telematics. Permira acquired a majority stake in the company in early 2020 for over $2.5 billion. As of mid-2025, Permira remains the lead investor, with a Permira partner recently quoted in July 2025 regarding the appointment of a new CEO.

permira::Tricentis.notes: Tricentis is a real technology company founded in Vienna, Austria, in 2007. However, it is not a portfolio company of Permira. It is currently a portfolio company of Insight Partners (which acquired a majority stake in 2017) and GTCR (which made a $1.33 billion investment in late 2024). Permira owns a similarly named company, Tricor, which is a professional services firm based in Hong Kong.

permira::Altasciences.notes: Altasciences is a real company headquartered in Laval, Canada, but it is not a portfolio company of Permira. It was acquired by Novo Holdings from Audax Private Equity in February 2021 and remains a Novo Holdings portfolio company as of early 2026. Permira owns other companies in the same sector, such as Ergomed and Quotient Sciences, which may be the source of the confusion.

permira::Sterling Pharma Solutions.notes: Sterling Pharma Solutions is a real CDMO headquartered in Dudley, UK. It is currently a portfolio company of GHO Capital (which acquired it in 2019) and Partners Group (which took a significant minority stake in 2023). While Permira Credit (formerly Permira Debt Managers) has provided debt financing and acted as a lender for the company's acquisitions and refinancing, Sterling Pharma Solutions is not an equity portfolio company of Permira's private equity funds.

permira::Synamedia.notes: Synamedia is a video technology company formed in 2018 when Permira acquired Cisco's Service Provider Video Software Solutions (SPVSS) business. It is headquartered in Staines-upon-Thames, UK, and remains a current portfolio company in Permira's technology sector as of 2025.

permira::Squarespace.notes: Permira completed its $7.2 billion take-private acquisition of Squarespace on October 17, 2024. The company is currently held in Permira's technology portfolio.

permira::BioCatch.notes: BioCatch is a Tel Aviv-based cybersecurity company specializing in behavioral biometrics. Permira (via its Growth Opportunities fund) acquired a majority stake in the company in May 2024 at a $1.3 billion valuation, with the transaction officially closing in September 2024. It is currently a portfolio company.

permira::Corin Group.notes: Corin Group is a UK-based orthopaedic company headquartered in Cirencester. It was acquired by Permira in May 2018 and remains a current portfolio company as of early 2025, with recent company announcements (April 2024) still identifying Permira as the parent company.

permira::Teraco.notes: Teraco is a South African data center provider. Permira acquired it in 2015 and sold its majority stake to Digital Realty in a deal that closed in August 2022, though Permira retained a minority interest.

permira::LegalZoom.notes: LegalZoom was a portfolio company of Permira starting in 2014 when Permira acquired a majority stake. The company is headquartered in Glendale, CA, and operates in the legal technology/SaaS sector. Permira exited its investment following LegalZoom's IPO on June 30, 2021.

permira::Topcast.notes: Topcast Aviation Supplies is a Hong Kong-based aerospace company. Permira acquired a majority stake in 2019 but exited the investment in November 2025 when it was sold to Warburg Pincus.

permira::Ames Taping Tools.notes: Ames Taping Tools is a real company headquartered in Suwanee, GA, but it was never a portfolio company of Permira. Its ownership history includes Aurora Capital Group (2005–2017) and Sun Capital Partners (2017–2021), before it was acquired by GMS Inc. in 2021. The claim likely confuses it with DiversiTech, a company in the same sector and location (Suwanee/Duluth, GA) that was a portfolio company of Permira until its sale to Partners Group in 2021.

permira::DiversiTech.notes: DiversiTech (headquartered in Duluth, GA) was acquired by Permira in 2017. In December 2021, Permira sold its majority stake to Partners Group for $2.2 billion, while retaining a minority interest.

permira::Full Truck Alliance.notes: Full Truck Alliance (also known as Manbang Group) is a real digital freight platform headquartered in Guiyang, China. Permira, through its Growth Opportunities Fund I, co-led a $1.7 billion funding round in the company in November 2020. Although the company went public on the NYSE in June 2021 (ticker: YMM), Permira entities (such as Permira PGO1 SPV Limited) continue to be listed as shareholders in the company's 2024 and 2025 SEC filings, indicating the investment has not been fully exited.

permira::Kroll.notes: Permira acquired Duff & Phelps in 2018, which subsequently acquired Kroll and rebranded under that name. In 2020, Permira sold a majority stake to a consortium led by Stone Point Capital and Further Global but retained a minority equity stake and board representation, maintaining its status as a portfolio company.

permira::TMF Group.notes: TMF Group is a real company headquartered in Amsterdam, but it is a portfolio company of CVC Capital Partners and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), not Permira. Permira expressed interest in acquiring the company in 2016 but was unsuccessful; CVC acquired it in 2017.

permira::GGW Group.notes: GGW Group is a Hamburg-based insurance brokerage platform. Permira acquired a co-controlling stake in the company from Hg in a transaction that closed on April 24, 2024. As of early 2025, it remains a current portfolio company of both Permira and Hg.

permira::Lowell.notes: Lowell (Lowell Group) is a major credit management company headquartered in Leeds, UK. It was acquired by Permira in 2015 (merging it with GFKL) and remains a current portfolio company as of February 2026, following a significant recapitalization in mid-2025 where Permira and OTPP maintained their ownership.

permira::Evelyn Partners.notes: Evelyn Partners is a major UK wealth management firm. Permira has been its majority owner since 2014 (originally through Bestinvest/Tilney). On February 9, 2026, Permira and Warburg Pincus announced an agreement to sell Evelyn Partners to NatWest Group for £2.7 billion. As the deal is expected to close in summer 2026, it remains a current portfolio company as of February 2026.

permira::GoCardless.notes: GoCardless is a London-based fintech company. Permira (via its Growth Opportunities fund) led a $312 million Series G round in February 2022. Although an acquisition by Mollie was announced in December 2025, the deal is expected to close in mid-2026, so the investment is still currently held.

permira::Carta.notes: Carta is a San Francisco-based financial technology company. Permira invested in Carta in 2021 through its Permira Growth Opportunities (PGO) strategy. As of early 2026, Carta continues to be listed as an active portfolio company in Permira's official communications and industry databases.

permira::Canoe Intelligence.notes: Canoe Intelligence is a real fintech company based in New York, but it is not a portfolio company of Permira. Its major investors include Goldman Sachs (which led its Series C in 2024), Blackstone Innovations Investments, Carlyle Group, Nasdaq Ventures, and Hamilton Lane. Permira is a private equity firm that owns Alter Domus, which has a strategic partnership with Canoe Intelligence, but Permira itself does not hold an equity stake in Canoe.

permira::Evri.notes: Evri (formerly Hermes UK) is a portfolio company of Apollo Global Management, which acquired it from Advent International in August 2024. Permira has no record of owning the company.

permira::Flix.notes: Flix SE (formerly FlixMobility) is a Munich-based transportation company. Permira invested in the company in 2019 via its Growth Opportunities fund. As of late 2024 and early 2025, Permira remains a shareholder, and its partner Stefan Dziarski continues to serve on the Flix Supervisory Board following a 35% minority stake acquisition by EQT and Kühne Holding in July 2024.

permira::BestSecret.notes: BestSecret (and its parent company Schustermann & Borenstein) was acquired by Permira in 2016. As of February 2026, it remains a portfolio company of Permira, although reports in early 2024 indicated the firm was exploring exit options such as a sale or IPO.

pai-partners::Angulas Aguinaga.notes: Angulas Aguinaga is a real food company headquartered in Irura, Spain. PAI Partners acquired a majority stake in the company in November 2020 through its Mid-Market Fund (PAI MMF) and it remains a current portfolio company as of February 2026.

pai-partners::Armacell.notes: Armacell is a Luxembourg-based industrial manufacturing company specializing in insulation and engineered foams. It was acquired by PAI Partners (as majority shareholder) and KIRKBI in February 2020 and remains a current portfolio company in PAI Europe VII.

pai-partners::Labeyrie Fine Foods.notes: Labeyrie Fine Foods is a French gourmet food company headquartered in Saint-Geours-de-Maremne. PAI Partners acquired a significant stake in the company in 2014 and remains a co-owner alongside the Lur Berri cooperative as of early 2025.

pai-partners::Looping Group.notes: Looping Group is a French leisure park operator. PAI Partners acquired a majority stake in the company in 2023 from Mubadala Capital and Bpifrance. It is currently held in the PAI Partners VIII fund.

bc-partners::Keter.notes: Keter Group was a portfolio company of BC Partners from 2016 until early 2024. Following a failed sale process and debt restructuring, ownership was transferred to the company's senior lenders in March 2024, effectively ending BC Partners' equity control.

bc-partners::GardaWorld.notes: GardaWorld is a real security services company headquartered in Montreal. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in 2019 and completed a sale of that majority interest in early 2025 (recapitalization valued at C$13.5bn-C$14bn). However, BC Partners retains a minority stake in the company, making its status 'current' as a partial holding.

bc-partners::Presidio.notes: Presidio is a real IT services company headquartered in New York. BC Partners acquired it in 2019 but sold a majority stake to Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in April 2024. While BC Partners retains a minority interest, they officially list the investment status as 'Realised' with an exit year of 2024.

bc-partners::PetSmart.notes: PetSmart is a real company headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. It was acquired by a consortium led by BC Partners in 2015 for $8.7 billion. As of late 2023 and into 2025, BC Partners remains the majority shareholder, even after Apollo Global Management took a strategic minority stake in the company in late 2023.

bc-partners::Chewy.notes: Chewy is a major online pet retailer headquartered in Dania Beach, FL. BC Partners acquired it through its portfolio company PetSmart in 2017. While Chewy went public in 2019 and BC Partners has since sold several large blocks of shares (including a $1 billion sale in mid-2025), as of February 2026, BC Partners remains the largest shareholder with approximately 42.5% ownership and significant voting power. Therefore, the status is 'current' (or partially realized) rather than fully 'exited'.

bc-partners::Springer Nature.notes: Springer Nature is a major academic publishing company headquartered in Berlin. BC Partners acquired a stake in its predecessor (Springer Science+Business Media) in 2013 and helped form the current entity through a merger in 2015. Although Springer Nature completed an initial public offering (IPO) on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in October 2024, BC Partners retained a significant minority stake (approximately 36% post-IPO), meaning it remains a current portfolio company.

bc-partners::United Group.notes: United Group is a major telecommunications and media operator in Southeast Europe, headquartered in Hoofddorp (Amsterdam area), Netherlands. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in the company from KKR in March 2019. As of early 2026, it remains a portfolio company of BC Partners, although the group has recently divested several non-EU assets to focus on its European Union markets.

bc-partners::Valtech.notes: Valtech is a global digital services agency headquartered in London. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in the company in July 2021 for a valuation of approximately $1.4 billion. As of early 2026, it remains an unrealised investment in BC Partners' private equity portfolio.

bc-partners::Pharmathen.notes: Pharmathen was acquired by BC Partners in 2015, but the firm sold its majority stake to Partners Group in July 2021 for approximately €1.6 billion.

bc-partners::GFL Environmental.notes: GFL Environmental is a real company (Waste Management/Environmental Services). BC Partners invested in 2018 and remains a major shareholder following its 2020 IPO (listed as 'Partially Realised'). Additionally, in March 2025, BC Partners acquired a 28% stake in GFL's divested Environmental Services division (GES), which is currently an 'Unrealised' investment.

bc-partners::VetPartners.notes: VetPartners is a UK-based veterinary group headquartered in York. It was acquired by BC Partners in November 2018 from August Equity and Ares Management. As of early 2026, it remains an unrealized investment in BC Partners' portfolio, despite reports in late 2022 and 2023 that the firm was considering a sale. Note that a separate entity also named VetPartners operates in Australia and New Zealand and was acquired by EQT in 2023.

bc-partners::Teneo.notes: Teneo is a real professional services firm headquartered in New York. BC Partners acquired a minority stake in the company in 2015 but exited the investment in June 2019 by selling its shareholding to CVC Capital Partners.

bc-partners::Dummen Orange.notes: Dümmen Orange is a real company headquartered in De Lier, Netherlands. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in 2015. In May 2024, a restructuring deal was announced where a group of lenders (including ICG and J.P. Morgan) took over majority ownership, but BC Partners remains a minority investor and still lists the company in its portfolio.

bc-partners::Zest Dental Solutions.notes: Zest Dental Solutions, headquartered in Carlsbad, USA, was acquired by BC Partners in February 2018 from Avista Capital Partners. As of early 2026, it remains an active portfolio company within BC Partners' healthcare sector.

bc-partners::Synthon.notes: Synthon is a real pharmaceutical company headquartered in Nijmegen. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in 2019. In late 2024, BC Partners reached an agreement to sell the majority stake to Goldman Sachs Alternatives (transaction closed in 2025), but BC Partners retained a minority stake in the company, meaning it remains a portfolio company.

bc-partners::Women's Care Enterprises.notes: Women's Care Enterprises is a real healthcare company headquartered in Tampa, FL. BC Partners acquired it from Lindsay Goldberg in December 2020 and it remains a current (unrealized) portfolio company in their North American healthcare sector.

bc-partners::Havea.notes: Havea Group is a French natural healthcare company headquartered in Boufféré. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in the company from 3i Group in October 2022 for approximately €1.1 billion and it remains a current (unrealized) investment in their portfolio.

bc-partners::CloudBees.notes: CloudBees is a real enterprise software company headquartered in San Jose, California. However, it is not a portfolio company of BC Partners. It is currently a portfolio company of Bridgepoint Group (specifically Bridgepoint Capital and Bridgepoint Credit), which led its $150 million Series F funding round in December 2021. The claim likely confuses BC Partners with Bridgepoint, both of which are major European private equity firms.

bc-partners::Cision.notes: Cision is a real company headquartered in Chicago, but it is a portfolio company of Platinum Equity, not BC Partners. Platinum Equity acquired Cision in January 2020 for approximately $2.7 billion. The confusion may arise because BC Partners' press releases are frequently distributed via PR Newswire, which is a Cision subsidiary.

bc-partners::Efront.notes: Efront is a real financial technology company headquartered in Paris. However, it was never a portfolio company of BC Partners. It was owned by Francisco Partners (2011–2015) and then Bridgepoint (2015–2019) before being acquired by BlackRock in 2019. BC Partners is a known user of Efront's software, which may be the source of the confusion.

bc-partners::Navex Global.notes: Navex Global is a GRC software company headquartered in Lake Oswego, Oregon. BC Partners acquired a majority stake in the company in 2018. In October 2025, BC Partners completed the sale of its majority stake to a consortium led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Blackstone, though it retained a significant minority interest. The transaction is classified as an exit for BC Partners.

bc-partners::Ceva Santé Animale.notes: Ceva Santé Animale is a real veterinary pharmaceutical company headquartered in Libourne, France. While BC Partners was reported as a potential bidder for the company in 2014, it did not acquire it. The company is currently majority-owned by its management and employees, supported by a consortium of investors including Temasek, PSP Investments, Téthys Invest, and ARCHIMED (who joined in a 2025 funding round). BC Partners does own other assets in the pet sector, such as VetPartners and PetLab Co., but not Ceva.

bc-partners::Madison Safety & Flow.notes: Madison Safety & Flow is a business unit and subsidiary of Madison Industries, a large privately held company based in Chicago. BC Partners does not own Madison Safety & Flow; however, BC Partners does own a different company called Madison Logic (a digital marketing platform), which likely caused the confusion.

bc-partners::Comau.notes: Comau is a real industrial automation company headquartered in Turin, Italy. However, it is not a portfolio company of BC Partners. It was recently acquired by the private equity firm One Equity Partners (OEP), which completed the purchase of a majority stake from Stellantis on December 30, 2024.

bc-partners::Accudyne Industries.notes: Accudyne Industries was acquired by BC Partners and The Carlyle Group in 2012. The company, headquartered in Dallas, operated in the industrial manufacturing sector. It was exited through the sale of its three main business units: Sullair (sold to Hitachi in 2017), Precision Flow Systems (sold to Ingersoll-Rand in 2019), and Sundyne (sold to Warburg Pincus in 2020).

bc-partners::SGB-SMIT.notes: SGB-SMIT is a Regensburg-based transformer manufacturer. BC Partners acquired the company in 2008 and successfully exited the investment by selling it to One Equity Partners in 2017.

apax-partners::ThoughtSpot.notes: ThoughtSpot is a real enterprise analytics company headquartered in Sunnyvale, but it is not a portfolio company of Apax Partners. The claim likely confuses ThoughtSpot with ThoughtWorks, a software consultancy that was acquired by Apax in 2017 and taken private again in late 2024. ThoughtSpot's actual investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Silver Lake.

apax-partners::WGSN.notes: Apax Partners completed the acquisition of WGSN, a London-based trend forecasting company, from Ascential plc in February 2024 for approximately £700 million. As of February 2026, WGSN remains a portfolio company of the Apax XI Fund and recently expanded its own portfolio by acquiring IWSR in June 2025.

apax-partners::Vyaire Medical.notes: Vyaire Medical is a real company headquartered in Mettawa, IL. It was formed as a joint venture between Becton Dickinson and Apax Partners in 2016, with Apax taking 100% control in 2018. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2024 and has been selling off its business units (e.g., Consumables to SunMed in 2023 and RDx to Trudell Medical in 2024). As of February 2026, the bankruptcy process is ongoing, and it remains a portfolio company of Apax Partners, albeit as a distressed asset in liquidation.

apax-partners::Infogain.notes: Infogain is a digital platform and software engineering company headquartered in Los Gatos, California. It was acquired by funds advised by Apax Partners in June 2021 from ChrysCapital. As of July 2024, it remains a portfolio company of Apax Partners, recently acquiring Salesforce consulting firm Impaqtive.

apax-partners::Fractal Analytics.notes: Fractal Analytics (trading as Fractal) is a real AI and technology company with dual headquarters in Mumbai and New York. Apax Partners invested $200 million in the company in 2019 through its vehicle Quinag Bidco Ltd. As of February 2026, the company has recently completed an Initial Public Offering (IPO) on the Indian exchanges (listing on February 16, 2026). While Apax Partners sold a portion of its 18.64% stake in the Offer for Sale (OFS) during the IPO, it remains a significant shareholder, making the 'current' status accurate.

apax-partners::EcoOnline.notes: EcoOnline is a Norwegian-founded EHS and ESG software company that was acquired by Apax Partners (specifically the Apax X Fund) in June 2022. It is currently listed as an active portfolio company on the Apax Partners website and in recent financial news as of early 2026.

apax-partners::Ole Smoky Distillery.notes: Apax Partners acquired a controlling stake in Ole Smoky Distillery in March 2022 from Centerview Capital. The company is headquartered in Gatlinburg, Tennessee, and operates in the spirits (Food & Beverage) sector. As of early 2026, it remains a current portfolio company of Apax Partners.

apax-partners::Trade Me.notes: Trade Me is a major New Zealand online marketplace headquartered in Wellington. It was acquired by Apax Partners in May 2019 for NZ$2.56 billion and remains a current portfolio company as of February 2026, despite periodic rumors of a potential public listing.

apax-partners::Rodenstock.notes: Rodenstock is a Munich-based manufacturer of ophthalmic lenses and eyewear. It was acquired by Apax Partners in March 2021 from Compass Partners for approximately €1.5 billion. As of late 2025 and early 2026, it remains a current portfolio company of Apax Partners, as confirmed by Apax Global Alpha's financial reports and industry news.

apax-partners::Healthium.notes: Healthium Medtech (headquartered in Bangalore) was acquired by Apax Partners in 2018 and sold to KKR in May 2024 for approximately $839 million (Rs 7,000 crore).

apax-partners::MatchesFashion.notes: MatchesFashion was acquired by Apax Partners in 2017 and sold to Frasers Group in December 2023, confirming its exited status.

apax-partners::Inmarsat.notes: Inmarsat was acquired by a consortium led by Apax Partners and Warburg Pincus in December 2019. The company was subsequently sold to Viasat in May 2023, marking the exit for Apax.

apax-partners::Neuraxpharm.notes: Neuraxpharm was acquired by Apax Partners in 2016 (merged with Invent Farma) and was sold to Permira in 2020, confirming its status as an exited portfolio company.

apax-partners::LGC.notes: LGC (formerly the Laboratory of the Government Chemist) is a real life sciences company headquartered in Teddington, UK. However, it is not and has never been a portfolio company of Apax Partners. Its ownership history includes 3i, LGV Capital (2003-2010), Bridgepoint (2010-2015), and KKR (2015-2020). It is currently owned by a consortium led by Cinven and Astorg, who acquired it in 2020.

apax-partners::Duck Creek Technologies.notes: Duck Creek Technologies is a real insurance software company headquartered in Boston. Apax Partners acquired a majority stake in the company from Accenture in 2016, took it public in 2020, and fully exited its position in 2023 when the company was acquired by Vista Equity Partners for $2.6 billion.

apax-partners::Coalfire.notes: Coalfire is a cybersecurity advisory and assessment firm headquartered in Westminster, Colorado. It was acquired by funds advised by Apax Partners in April 2020 and remains a current portfolio company in their Tech sector.

apax-partners::SavATree.notes: SavATree is a professional tree and lawn care company headquartered in Bedford Hills, NY. It was acquired by Apax Partners (specifically the Apax X Fund) from CI Capital Partners in late 2021 and remains a current portfolio company in Apax's services sector.

apax-partners::Cadence Education.notes: Cadence Education is a Scottsdale-based provider of early childhood education. It was acquired by Apax Partners from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners in March 2020 and remains a current portfolio company as of February 2026, continuing to make add-on acquisitions under Apax ownership.

apax-partners::Genius Sports.notes: Genius Sports was a portfolio company of Apax Partners starting in 2018. However, Apax fully exited its remaining equity stake in the company in July 2024, following its 2021 public listing on the NYSE.

apax-partners::Paycor.notes: Paycor is a Cincinnati-based HCM software company. Apax Partners acquired a majority stake in 2018 and exited the investment via a $4.1 billion sale to Paychex, Inc., which was announced in January 2025 and completed later that year.

apax-partners::Adevinta.notes: Adevinta is a real company headquartered in Oslo, but it is not a portfolio company of Apax Partners. It was taken private in 2024 by a consortium led by Blackstone and Permira (along with co-investors General Atlantic and TCV). Apax Partners has been a bidder for certain Adevinta assets (such as its Spanish unit and Distilled) during its subsequent breakup, but does not own the parent company.

apax-partners::Candela.notes: Candela (formerly Syneron Candela) is a medical aesthetic device company headquartered in Marlborough, MA. It was acquired by Apax Partners in July 2017 for approximately $400 million. As of early 2026, it remains a current portfolio company on the Apax website, although there have been reports of a potential sale or IPO.

apax-partners::Innovage.notes: InnovAge (InnovAge Holding Corp.) is a Denver-based healthcare provider specializing in PACE services. Apax Partners and Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe (WCAS) acquired the company in 2020 and took it public in March 2021 (NASDAQ: INNV). As of early 2026, Apax remains the majority shareholder and continues to list InnovAge as a current portfolio company on its website.

apax-partners::Bonterra.notes: Bonterra is an Austin-based social good software company formed in 2021 by Apax Partners through the merger of CyberGrants, EveryAction, Network for Good, and Social Solutions. As of early 2026, it remains a current portfolio company of Apax Partners.

apax-partners::Alcumus.notes: Alcumus is a Cardiff-based risk management technology company. Apax Partners acquired a controlling stake in the company in February 2022 from Inflexion. As of early 2025, Alcumus merged with Veriforce, another Apax portfolio company, and remains under Apax's ownership.

apax-partners::Barentz.notes: Barentz is a real company headquartered in Hoofddorp, Netherlands, specializing in life science ingredients (Pharma, Food, etc.). However, it is a portfolio company of Cinven, not Apax Partners. Cinven acquired Barentz in 2019 and recently moved it into a continuation fund in 2024 to extend its holding period. Apax Partners owns a direct competitor in the same sector, Azelis.

apax-partners::GlobalLogic.notes: GlobalLogic was acquired by Apax Partners in 2013. Apax exited the investment in two stages: selling a 48% stake to CPPIB in 2017 and the remaining stake to Partners Group in 2018. The company was subsequently acquired by Hitachi in 2021.

apax-partners::Sophos.notes: Sophos is a real cybersecurity company headquartered in Abingdon, UK. Apax Partners acquired a majority stake in 2010 for approximately $830 million. The firm exited its investment following Sophos's IPO on the London Stock Exchange in 2015. Sophos was subsequently acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2020.

apax-partners::Unilabs.notes: Unilabs is a Geneva-based healthcare diagnostics company. It was a portfolio company of Apax Partners (initially invested in 2007, majority control in 2017) and was sold to A.P. Moller Holding in a deal announced in December 2021 and completed in early 2022.

apax-partners::Signavio.notes: Signavio is a Berlin-based business process management software company. Apax Digital (the growth equity arm of Apax Partners) led a $177 million investment in the company in July 2019. The investment was exited in March 2021 when Signavio was acquired by SAP for approximately €950 million.

apax-partners::Idealista.notes: Idealista is a real estate technology company headquartered in Madrid. Apax Partners (via Apax VIII) first acquired a majority stake in 2015 and exited to EQT in 2020. Apax X reinvested for a minority stake in 2021, which was sold to Cinven in a transaction that closed in December 2024.

tikehau-capital::Aubert & Duval.notes: Aubert & Duval was acquired in April 2023 by a consortium composed of Airbus, Safran, and Tikehau Capital (via its private equity arm). The three partners hold equal shares in the company.

tikehau-capital::GreenYellow.notes: GreenYellow is a French renewable energy company headquartered in Puteaux. Tikehau Capital (via its T2 Energy Transition Fund) initially invested in 2018. While Ardian acquired a majority stake in 2022, Tikehau Capital reinvested and remains a minority shareholder as of late 2024.

tikehau-capital::Odealim.notes: Odealim (formerly AssurCopro) is a French insurance broker that was a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital under its Private Debt (Credit) strategy. The investment was exited in September 2022 when the financing was repaid following a change in the company's ownership structure (Ardian acquired a co-controlling stake alongside TA Associates).

tikehau-capital::Ecore.notes: Ecore (Groupe Ecore) is a French recycling leader headquartered in Puteaux. Tikehau Capital (via Salvepar) was a minority investor alongside HIG Capital. The company was sold to Derichebourg in a transaction completed in early 2022.

tikehau-capital::Amutec.notes: Amutec S.r.l. is a real industrial manufacturing company based in Greve in Chianti, Italy. However, it is a portfolio company of Ambienta SGR (acquired in August 2019 and part of their REPAKT platform), not Tikehau Capital. Tikehau Capital is frequently mentioned in the same Italian private equity news roundups for unrelated deals (e.g., DoveVivo or Assiteca), which may be the source of the confusion.

tikehau-capital::Visiativ.notes: Visiativ (headquartered in Charbonnières-les-Bains) was a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, which first invested in May 2018. However, the company was exited in October 2024 following the acquisition of its controlling shareholder, Alliativ, by Groupe SNEF and a subsequent tender offer.

tikehau-capital::NGE.notes: NGE (Nouvelles Générations d'Entrepreneurs) is a major French construction group headquartered in Tarascon (Saint-Étienne-du-Grès). It is a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, though it is held within Tikehau's Private Debt (Credit) portfolio rather than its Private Equity arm. Tikehau has provided debt financing to NGE since 2014 and was recently involved in arranging credit lines for the company as of 2024/2025. The equity is currently held by Montefiore Investment (28%) and the company's founders, managers, and employees (72%).

tikehau-capital::Nexteam.notes: Nexteam Group is a French aerospace and defense company headquartered in Marmande. Tikehau Capital invested €114 million for a minority stake in May 2018 and continues to list the company in its private equity portfolio.

tikehau-capital::IREIT Global.notes: IREIT Global is a Singapore-listed real estate investment trust. Tikehau Capital and City Developments Limited (CDL) jointly own the REIT's manager (IREIT Global Group Pte. Ltd.). Tikehau Capital also holds a significant direct equity stake in the REIT (approximately 29%). As of mid-2025, Tikehau Capital remains a key sponsor and shareholder.

tikehau-capital::Euronext.notes: Euronext is a major European stock exchange group headquartered in Amsterdam. While Tikehau Capital is an asset management firm listed on Euronext Paris, Euronext itself is not and has not been a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. The claim likely confuses Euronext with Eurazeo, a private equity firm in which Tikehau Capital held a stake and fully exited in 2021.

tikehau-capital::Skeepers.notes: Skeepers (formerly known as Net Reviews or Avis Vérifiés) is a technology company headquartered in Marseille, France. Tikehau Capital invested in the company in December 2019 (alongside PSG Equity) through its growth equity fund. As of early 2026, Skeepers remains an active portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, with no record of a full exit.

tikehau-capital::Believe.notes: Believe (Believe SAS) is a real digital music company headquartered in Paris. However, it is not a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. It was historically backed by TCV (Technology Crossover Ventures), Ventech, and XAnge, and was taken private in 2024 by a consortium led by EQT and TCV. The confusion may stem from the fact that both Tikehau Capital and Believe are portfolio companies of the 'Fonds Stratégique de Participations' (FSP), or a naming confusion between TCV and Tikehau.

tikehau-capital::Forsee Power.notes: Forsee Power is a real French company specializing in smart battery systems for electric mobility, headquartered in the Paris region (Ivry-sur-Seine). Tikehau Capital invested in the company in 2020 through its T2 Energy Transition Fund. While Forsee Power went public (IPO) on Euronext Paris in November 2021, Tikehau Capital has remained a significant shareholder and continues to hold a seat on the board of directors as of 2024.

tikehau-capital::BioGroup.notes: BioGroup (or BioGroup-LCD) is a real French medical laboratory group headquartered in Courbevoie. While Tikehau Capital has significant exposure to BioGroup, it is through its credit and private debt funds (holding bonds and loans) rather than its private equity fund. The primary equity owners of BioGroup are Intermediate Capital Group (ICG), Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec (CDPQ), and the founder's family. Tikehau Capital's private equity portfolio includes a similarly named company, BioFirst (formerly Biobest), which may be the source of confusion.

tikehau-capital::Elsan.notes: Elsan is a major French healthcare group headquartered in Paris. However, it is not a private equity portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. Its primary private equity owners are KKR, CVC Capital Partners, Ardian, Tethys Invest, and Mérieux Equity Partners. Tikehau Capital is an investor in Elsan's competitor, Vivalto Santé, and has previously provided debt financing to Elsan through its credit/CLO funds, but does not hold an equity stake in its private equity portfolio.

tikehau-capital::Preligens.notes: Preligens is a Paris-based AI technology company founded in 2016. Tikehau Capital invested in the company in November 2020 through its Brienne III cybersecurity fund and completed its exit by selling its stake to Safran in September 2024 for an enterprise value of €220 million.

tikehau-capital::Trustpair.notes: Trustpair is a Paris-based fintech company specializing in fraud prevention. It is a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, which invested in Trustpair's €20 million Series B round in October 2022 through its cybersecurity-focused private equity fund, Brienne III (managed by Tikehau Ace Capital, now fully integrated into Tikehau Capital). As of late 2024, it remains a current holding.

tikehau-capital::Inovie.notes: Inovie is a real medical diagnostics company based in Montpellier. However, it is not a private equity portfolio company of Tikehau Capital; Tikehau is a lender providing debt financing (Term Loan B) to the group. The actual private equity owners are Ardian, GIC, APG, and Mubadala, who acquired a majority stake in 2020/2021.

tikehau-capital::Olygose.notes: Olygose (headquartered in Venette, France) was a portfolio company of Emertec Gestion, which was acquired by Tikehau Capital in 2017. However, Olygose was sold to the US-based company AIDP in September 2020, so its current status is exited rather than current.

tikehau-capital::Amarenco.notes: Amarenco is a renewable energy company headquartered in Cork, Ireland. Tikehau Capital initially invested in November 2020 and increased its position to a controlling stake in early 2023. As of February 2026, it remains listed as a portfolio company, although reports from April 2025 indicated that Tikehau was considering a potential sale of its stake in 2026.

tikehau-capital::Valorem.notes: Valorem (headquartered in Bègles, France, in the renewable energy sector) was a portfolio company of 3i Infrastructure, not Tikehau Capital. 3i Infrastructure acquired its stake in 2016 and exited in 2024, selling to a consortium led by AIP Management and IDIA. Tikehau Capital has invested in a different company called 'Ad Valorem' (real estate) and the renewable energy firm 'Amarenco', which may cause confusion.

tikehau-capital::Sateba.notes: Sateba is a real French industrial company specializing in concrete railway sleepers. However, it is not a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. It was previously owned by TowerBrook Capital Partners (acquired from Consolis in 2021) and was sold to the German rail technology group Vossloh in a deal announced in July 2024 and completed in October 2025. Tikehau Capital owns a competitor in the same sector called Alkern.

tikehau-capital::Mecachrome.notes: Mecachrome is a French aerospace and defense company headquartered in Amboise. tikehau-capital::Figeac Aéro.notes: Figeac Aéro is a French aerospace company headquartered in Figeac. Tikehau Capital, through its subsidiary Tikehau Ace Capital (formerly Ace Capital Partners), acquired a significant minority stake (approximately 26%) in the company between 2021 and 2022 as part of a financial restructuring. As of early 2025, Tikehau Capital remains a major shareholder and lists Figeac Aéro as a current portfolio company.

tikehau-capital::Aresia.notes: Aresia (formerly known as Rafaut) is a French aerospace and defense company headquartered in Villeneuve-la-Garenne. It is currently a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital (specifically through its subsidiary Tikehau Ace Capital), which reinvested in the company in 2018 alongside majority shareholder HLD Europe.

tikehau-capital::Wavestone.notes: Wavestone is a real, publicly traded management consulting firm based in Paris (Euronext: WAVE). It is not a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital; rather, it is controlled by its founders (the Imbert and Dancoisne families) and the former shareholders of Q_PERIOR. While Wavestone has provided strategic advisory services for deals involving Tikehau Capital, it is an independent entity.

tikehau-capital::Babilou.notes: Babilou (Babilou Family) is a real company headquartered in Bois-Colombes, France. Tikehau Capital was a private equity investor (via its Fund IV) but exited its equity stake in November 2020 when Antin Infrastructure Partners became the majority shareholder. However, Tikehau Capital remains a creditor, holding debt instruments (Term Loan B) in the company as of 2025.

tikehau-capital::Odyssey Education.notes: Odyssey Education (also known as Odyssey Group) is a Paris-based international education group founded in 2019. It is a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, which provided €20 million in debt financing (Credit expertise) in February 2023. It is currently listed as an active portfolio company on Tikehau Capital's official website.

tikehau-capital::Altrad.notes: Altrad is a real company headquartered in Montpellier, France, specializing in industrial services and construction equipment. Tikehau Capital is a current minority shareholder (holding a portion of a 3.05% stake alongside Arkea Capital) as of February 2026, according to S&P Global Ratings reports. While Tikehau's website lists a 2013 credit investment as 'exited' in November 2020, recent financial disclosures confirm a continuing equity position.

tikehau-capital::DWS Group.notes: DWS Group is a major German asset manager headquartered in Frankfurt and is a publicly traded company (MDAX listed). While Tikehau Capital participated in DWS's 2018 IPO as an anchor investor (initially holding a ~3% stake) and maintains a strategic alliance with the firm, DWS is classified as a 'listed investment' on Tikehau's balance sheet rather than a portfolio company of its private equity funds. As of late 2020, Tikehau had reduced its stake to approximately 0.51%, and the majority owner remains Deutsche Bank (~79.5%).

tikehau-capital::Mediobanca.notes: Mediobanca is a major Italian investment bank headquartered in Milan. It is not a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. Instead, Mediobanca frequently acts as a financial advisor or lead manager for Tikehau Capital's own deals and bond issuances. Furthermore, as of late 2025, Mediobanca was acquired by Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS), which now holds a controlling stake of approximately 86%.

tikehau-capital::Elvia PCB.notes: Elvia PCB (which rebranded to 'elvia electronics' in October 2024) was acquired by Tikehau Ace Capital in April 2022. It is currently held in Tikehau Capital's private equity portfolio within the Aerospace & Defence sector and is headquartered in Coutances, France.

tikehau-capital::WeAre Group.notes: WeAre Group is a real company headquartered in Montauban, France, operating in the Aerospace & Defence sector. In August 2022, it was acquired by Mecachrome in a merger backed by Tikehau Capital (specifically through its subsidiary Tikehau Ace Capital) and Bpifrance. Tikehau Capital currently holds a 64.3% majority stake in the combined group, and as of early 2026, the investment remains active.

tikehau-capital::Neoen.notes: Neoen is a real French renewable energy company, but it was not a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital. It was primarily a portfolio company of Impala (Jacques Veyrat's holding company) and the Fonds Stratégique de Participations (FSP). Tikehau Capital is often confused with Neoen because Tikehau held a stake in a similar competitor, Total Eren, which it exited in 2023. Neoen itself was recently acquired by Brookfield in late 2024/early 2025.

tikehau-capital::Inetum.notes: Inetum (formerly Gfi Informatique) was a portfolio company of Tikehau Capital, primarily within its private debt (credit) portfolio. Tikehau invested in December 2020 and exited in July 2022 following the acquisition of Inetum by Bain Capital from Mannai Corporation. The company is indeed headquartered in Saint-Ouen, France, and operates in the technology/digital services sector.

tikehau-capital::Selectirente.notes: Selectirente is a French listed real estate company (SIIC) specializing in city-center commercial properties. Tikehau Capital acquired a majority stake in the company between 2018 and 2019. As of early 2026, Tikehau Capital and its subsidiary Sofidy remain the majority shareholders and managers of Selectirente.

eurazeo::ManoMano.notes: ManoMano is a Paris-based e-commerce platform specializing in DIY and gardening. Eurazeo (specifically Eurazeo Growth) first invested in the company in 2019 and continues to list it as an active portfolio company on its official website.

eurazeo::Vestiaire Collective.notes: Vestiaire Collective is a real company headquartered in Paris. Eurazeo (via its Growth/Croissance arm) first invested in 2015 and has participated in several subsequent rounds, including the 2021 funding that granted the company unicorn status. As of February 2026, Eurazeo continues to list Vestiaire Collective as an active portfolio company.

eurazeo::Doctolib.notes: Doctolib is a prominent French healthcare technology company founded in 2013. Eurazeo (specifically through its Eurazeo Growth team) first invested in Doctolib in 2017 and has participated in multiple subsequent funding rounds, including the Series G round in 2022. Recent reports from late 2025 and early 2026 continue to list Doctolib as a major active portfolio company of Eurazeo.

eurazeo::Contentsquare.notes: Contentsquare is a Paris-based digital experience analytics company. Eurazeo first invested in 2019 (leading the Series C) and has participated in subsequent rounds, including the Series F in 2022. As of February 2026, it remains a significant holding in Eurazeo's growth portfolio.

eurazeo::PayFit.notes: PayFit is a Paris-based HR and payroll software company. Eurazeo (specifically through its Growth and Large Venture funds) has been a key investor since leading its Series C round in 2019 and participating in subsequent Series D (2021) and Series E (2022) rounds. As of early 2026, PayFit remains a private company in Eurazeo's portfolio.

eurazeo::Aroma-Zone.notes: Aroma-Zone is a French natural beauty and wellness company. Eurazeo acquired a majority stake in the company in July 2021 for approximately €414 million. In May 2025, Eurazeo sold about 20% of its stake to a secondary fund as part of an asset rotation plan but remains a primary shareholder. As of February 2026, no full exit has been completed.

eurazeo::Planet.notes: Planet (formerly Fintrax Group) is a payments and financial services company headquartered in Galway, Ireland. Eurazeo acquired the company in 2015. In 2021, Advent International acquired a stake, and the two firms now co-control the company. As of May 2025, Eurazeo continues to hold Planet as a portfolio asset.

eurazeo::I-Tracing.notes: I-Tracing is a French cybersecurity services provider headquartered in Puteaux. Eurazeo initially invested in the company in May 2021. In November 2024, Eurazeo announced the transition of the investment to a continuation fund, where it remains an anchor investor in co-control with Oakley Capital, confirming its status as a current portfolio company.

eurazeo::DORC.notes: DORC (Dutch Ophthalmic Research Center), headquartered in Zuidland, was acquired by Eurazeo in 2019 and successfully sold to Carl Zeiss Meditec AG in April 2024 for approximately €985 million.

eurazeo::Asmodee.notes: Asmodee is a major board game publisher headquartered in Guyancourt, France. It was a portfolio company of Eurazeo from 2014 until October 2018, when it was sold to PAI Partners for approximately €1.2 billion. It has since been sold again to Embracer Group.

eurazeo::Seqens.notes: Seqens (formerly known as Novacap) was acquired by Eurazeo in June 2016. Eurazeo finalized the sale of its majority stake to SK Capital Partners in December 2021, though its managed fund 'Nov Santé' retained a minority reinvestment. The company is headquartered in Écully, France, and operates in the pharmaceutical and specialty chemicals sector.

eurazeo::Exotec.notes: Exotec is a French warehouse robotics company headquartered in Croix. It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo, having received investment through Eurazeo's venture and growth divisions (including Idinvest Partners, which was acquired by Eurazeo). As of early 2026, it remains a current holding in Eurazeo's portfolio.

eurazeo::Swile.notes: Swile is a French fintech company headquartered in Montpellier. It is currently listed as an active portfolio company on Eurazeo's official website under its 'Venture - Digital' strategy, following investments in multiple funding rounds (Series C and D).

eurazeo::Electra.notes: Electra is a Paris-based electric vehicle fast-charging company. Eurazeo first invested in June 2022 and significantly increased its stake in January 2024 through its Eurazeo Transition Infrastructure Fund (ETIF). It remains a current portfolio company as of early 2026.

eurazeo::WorldStrides.notes: WorldStrides is an education travel company headquartered in Charlottesville, Virginia. Eurazeo acquired a majority stake in 2017. Although the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020 due to the pandemic, Eurazeo and Primavera Capital Group retained 100% ownership through the restructuring process. Eurazeo's financial reports from 2025 and early 2026 continue to list WorldStrides as a portfolio company.

eurazeo::Adjust.notes: Adjust is a Berlin-based mobile analytics company. Eurazeo Growth led a $227 million funding round in Adjust in 2019 and exited its stake when the company was acquired by AppLovin in April 2021 for approximately $1 billion.

eurazeo::MessageBird.notes: MessageBird (rebranded as Bird in 2024) is a cloud communications company headquartered in Amsterdam. Eurazeo Growth co-led a $1 billion Series C extension for the company in April 2021 and currently lists it as an active portfolio company.

eurazeo::PPRO.notes: PPRO is a London-based fintech company specializing in digital payments infrastructure. Eurazeo (via its Eurazeo Growth fund) first invested in PPRO in January 2021 and participated in a follow-on funding round in March 2024. It remains an active portfolio company.

eurazeo::Lumapps.notes: LumApps is a real technology company headquartered in Lyon, France. While it was a portfolio company of Eurazeo (invested since 2017), Eurazeo announced the sale of its stake to Bridgepoint in May 2024. The transaction closed in July 2024, making it an exited investment.

eurazeo::Gorgias.notes: Gorgias is a San Francisco-based technology company providing a customer service platform for e-commerce. It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo, largely through Eurazeo's acquisition of Idinvest Partners, which was a lead or significant investor in Gorgias's funding rounds (including its Series C). As of early 2026, the company remains private and active with no reported exit.

eurazeo::Malt.notes: Malt is a Paris-based freelance marketplace platform. Eurazeo co-led an €80 million Series C funding round in June 2021 and continues to list Malt as an active portfolio company on its official website as of 2025/2026.

eurazeo::Aiven.notes: Aiven is a Helsinki-based technology company specializing in managed open-source data infrastructure. Eurazeo (specifically Eurazeo Growth) led Aiven's $210 million Series D funding round in May 2022 and remains a current investor.

eurazeo::Neo4j.notes: Neo4j is a graph database company headquartered in San Mateo, California. Eurazeo led a $325 million Series F funding round for the company in June 2021 and currently lists Neo4j as an active portfolio company on its official website.

eurazeo::Amolyt Pharma.notes: Amolyt Pharma, headquartered in Lyon (Ecully), France, was a portfolio company of Kurma Partners, which is a subsidiary of Eurazeo. The company was acquired by AstraZeneca in July 2024 for approximately $1.05 billion.

eurazeo::TreeFrog Therapeutics.notes: TreeFrog Therapeutics is a French biotechnology company headquartered in Bordeaux (specifically Pessac/Talence). It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo, having received investment from Idinvest Partners (which was acquired by and integrated into Eurazeo) during its Series A round in 2019. The company remains in Eurazeo's venture/growth portfolio as of 2025, following subsequent funding rounds including a Series B in 2021 and financing from the European Investment Bank in 2025.

eurazeo::Alentis Therapeutics.notes: Alentis Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotech company headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo through its Nov Santé fund, which is managed by Eurazeo and holds a board observer seat at Alentis. The company remains in the portfolio following a significant $181.4 million Series D financing round in November 2024.

eurazeo::Dutch EyeCare Group.notes: Dutch EyeCare Group (EyeCare Groep) is a real company, but it is a portfolio company of EMK Capital, which acquired it in 2021. The claim likely confuses it with Dutch Ophthalmic Research Center (DORC), a different Dutch healthcare company that was a portfolio company of Eurazeo until it was sold to Carl Zeiss Meditec in April 2024.

eurazeo::Imcheck Therapeutics.notes: ImCheck Therapeutics was a portfolio company of Eurazeo, which invested both directly and through its subsidiary Kurma Partners. The company was acquired by the pharmaceutical group Ipsen in December 2025 for an upfront payment of €350 million and total potential milestones of up to €1 billion.

eurazeo::Thought Machine.notes: Thought Machine is a London-based fintech company. Eurazeo (via Eurazeo Growth) first invested in its Series B round in July 2020 and followed on in subsequent Series C (2021) and Series D (2022) rounds. As of February 2026, it remains a private company with Eurazeo listed as a current investor.

eurazeo::Reden Solar.notes: Reden Solar is a renewable energy company headquartered in Roquefort, France. Eurazeo was a shareholder from 2010 and completed the sale of its remaining 47% stake to a consortium led by Macquarie Asset Management in July 2022.

eurazeo::Ikaros Solar.notes: Eurazeo acquired a majority stake (80%) in Ikaros Solar in January 2022 and reportedly moved to full ownership in 2024. The company, headquartered in Schoten, Belgium, rebranded to Radiance Energy in September 2024 but remains an active portfolio company within Eurazeo's infrastructure strategy.

eurazeo::Etix Everywhere.notes: Etix Everywhere is a Luxembourg-based edge data center provider. Eurazeo invested in the company in February 2023 via its Transition Infrastructure Fund. As of late 2024, it remains a portfolio company, with Eurazeo sharing joint control alongside Infranity following a 2024 transaction.

eurazeo::I-Pulse.notes: I-Pulse Inc. is a real company specializing in pulsed-power technology for industrial manufacturing and mining. Eurazeo (specifically through its Eurazeo Growth division) invested in the company in 2012 and continues to list it as a portfolio company in its 2023 and 2024 financial reports. Recent data from 2025 and 2026 confirms it remains a private company with Eurazeo as a shareholder, alongside other major investors like BHP and Codelco. Its main research and manufacturing facilities are located in Toulouse, France.

eurazeo::Suez.notes: Suez SA is a major French water and waste management company, but it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. Following its acquisition by Veolia in 2022, a 'new Suez' was formed, which is currently owned by a consortium consisting of Meridiam (40%), Global Infrastructure Partners (40%), and the Caisse des Dépôts Group (20%). Eurazeo is not a member of this consortium, and there is no record of it holding a stake in Suez in its current or recent portfolio.

eurazeo::Orolia.notes: Orolia was a portfolio company of Eurazeo (specifically within its Small-mid buyout team) from 2016 until July 2022, when Eurazeo completed the sale of its majority stake to Safran. The company is a leader in Resilient Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) solutions and is headquartered in the Sophia Antipolis technology park (Valbonne), France.

eurazeo::Vitaprotech.notes: Vitaprotech (formerly ST Group) was acquired by Eurazeo PME in July 2018. Eurazeo exited the investment in 2022 by selling its majority stake to Apax Partners (now Seven2). The company is headquartered in Vaulx-en-Velin (Lyon region) and specializes in electronic security solutions.

eurazeo::Resource.notes: Resource (often stylized as ReSource Denmark) is a joint venture between Eurazeo and Quantafuel. It operates a large-scale plastic waste sorting facility in Esbjerg, Denmark, and is a portfolio company of the Eurazeo Transition Infrastructure Fund (ETIF).

eurazeo::Eovolt.notes: Eovolt (legal name Lion Distribution) is a real company based in Lyon, France, specializing in folding electric bikes. However, it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. eurazeo::Mediawan.notes: Mediawan is a real French media conglomerate, but it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. It was taken private in 2020 by a consortium led by KKR, Bpifrance, MACSF, and its founders (Xavier Niel, Matthieu Pigasse, and Pierre-Antoine Capton). Recent reports from 2024-2026 continue to identify KKR as the primary private equity backer.

eurazeo::Grand Frais.notes: Grand Frais (operated by Prosol) is a real French retail company headquartered in Givors. While Eurazeo (via its subsidiary Idinvest) was a minority investor in 2016, it exited its stake in 2017 when Ardian acquired a majority of the company. In December 2025, Ardian sold its majority stake to Apollo Global Management.

eurazeo::Waterdrop.notes: Waterdrop (Waterdrop Microdrink GmbH) is a real company based in Vienna, Austria, in the Food & Beverage sector. However, it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. Eurazeo's portfolio includes 'Waterloo Sparkling Water' (US) and 'Water Direct' (UK), which likely causes confusion. The Austrian Waterdrop's main investors include Temasek, Bitburger Ventures, and Founders Future.

eurazeo::StockX.notes: StockX is a real e-commerce company headquartered in Detroit, USA. However, it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. Eurazeo is a major investor in StockX's competitor, Vestiaire Collective, and in a similarly named retail technology company called Stockly. Major investors in StockX include Tiger Global, General Atlantic, and GV (Google Ventures).

eurazeo::Glossier.notes: Glossier is a real beauty company based in New York, but it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. Its primary investors include Lone Pine Capital, IVP, Sequoia Capital, and Forerunner Ventures. Eurazeo has invested in other beauty brands like Pat McGrath Labs (exited), Gisou, and Beekman 1802, which may lead to confusion.

eurazeo::Pat McGrath Labs.notes: Eurazeo (via Eurazeo Brands) invested $60 million in Pat McGrath Labs in July 2018, valuing the company at $1 billion. However, Eurazeo quietly exited its minority stake in 2021. The company has since faced financial difficulties and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 2026.

eurazeo::Herschel Supply Co..notes: Eurazeo Brands (a division of Eurazeo) completed a $60 million minority investment in Herschel Supply Co. in December 2019 as part of a consortium with Alliance Consumer Growth and HOOPP Capital Partners. There have been no reports of an exit, and recent news from late 2023 still identifies Eurazeo as a current investor.

eurazeo::Gisou.notes: Eurazeo completed a minority investment in Gisou in April 2022 through its Eurazeo Brands division. Gisou is a premium haircare and beauty company headquartered in Almere, Netherlands. There is no evidence of an exit, and it remains listed as a portfolio company.

eurazeo::Erewhon.notes: Erewhon is a real upscale grocery chain based in Los Angeles. However, it is a portfolio company of Stripes Group (which acquired a substantial minority stake in 2019), not Eurazeo. Eurazeo has invested in brands sold at Erewhon (such as Deux Foods), which may be the source of the confusion.

eurazeo::Beekman 1802.notes: Eurazeo acquired a majority stake in Beekman 1802 in December 2021 for $62 million (out of a total $92 million investment). The company is a clean beauty brand headquartered in Sharon Springs, NY, and is still listed as a portfolio company in 2026 reports.

eurazeo::Sommet Education.notes: Sommet Education is a leading hospitality and culinary arts education group headquartered in Clarens, Switzerland. It was acquired by Eurazeo in 2016. Despite reports of a potential sale process starting in late 2021, Eurazeo's 2023 and 2024 financial documents and Sommet's own 2025 press releases continue to identify it as a Eurazeo portfolio company.

eurazeo::Farfetch.notes: Farfetch is a luxury fashion e-commerce platform headquartered in London. Eurazeo invested in the company in May 2016 via its Eurazeo Growth division and announced the sale of its entire stake in November 2020.

eurazeo::Charlotte Tilbury.notes: Charlotte Tilbury is a real company, but it was never a portfolio company of Eurazeo. It was primarily backed by Sequoia Capital and Venrex before being acquired by the Spanish group Puig in 2020. The claim likely confuses Charlotte Tilbury with Pat McGrath Labs, another high-end beauty brand that Eurazeo did invest in and subsequently exit.

eurazeo::Banijay Group.notes: Banijay Group (now part of FL Entertainment) was a portfolio company of Idinvest Partners, which was acquired by Eurazeo in 2018. The company is headquartered in Paris and operates in the Media & Entertainment sector. It went public on Euronext Amsterdam in 2022 via a merger with the SPAC Pegasus Entrepreneurs, which constitutes an exit for its private equity backers.

eurazeo::Picard.notes: Picard Surgelés is a major French frozen food retailer headquartered in Fontainebleau. Eurazeo was an investor in the company, having committed €50 million (notably through its Eurazeo Private Value fund) to support its growth alongside majority owners like Lion Capital. In January 2025, Invest Group Zouari (IGZ) completed the acquisition of 100% of Picard's capital, resulting in a full exit for previous shareholders, including Lion Capital and Eurazeo.

eurazeo::B&B Hotels.notes: B&B Hotels (headquartered in Brest, France) was a portfolio company of Eurazeo from 2005 until 2010, when it was sold to The Carlyle Group. It is currently owned by Goldman Sachs.

eurazeo::Qonto.notes: Qonto is a Paris-based fintech company providing banking services to SMEs. Eurazeo participated in Qonto's €486 million Series D funding round in January 2022 and continues to list the company as a major holding in its growth portfolio as of early 2026.

eurazeo::Alan.notes: Alan is a Paris-based digital health insurance company founded in 2016. It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo, primarily through Eurazeo's acquisition of Idinvest Partners in 2018, which was an early investor in Alan. Industry databases and Eurazeo's own reporting confirm its status as a current portfolio company, and it recently raised a Series F funding round in September 2024.

eurazeo::Younited Credit.notes: Younited Credit (Younited S.A.) is a French fintech company headquartered in Paris. Eurazeo is a major shareholder and has supported the company through multiple funding rounds. In late 2024, Younited went public via a business combination with Iris Financial S.A. (renamed Younited Financial S.A., ticker: YOUNI), and Eurazeo continues to hold a significant stake in the listed entity as of early 2026.

eurazeo::AlixPartners.notes: AlixPartners is a real global consulting firm headquartered in New York, but it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. eurazeo::Descartes Underwriting.notes: Descartes Underwriting is a Paris-based insurtech firm specializing in parametric insurance. Eurazeo co-led its $120 million Series B funding round in January 2022 and currently lists the company as an active portfolio company on its official website.

eurazeo::Mooncard.notes: Mooncard (Moongroup SAS) is a real French fintech company headquartered in Paris. However, it is not a portfolio company of Eurazeo. Its funding rounds (Series A, B, and C) were led or participated in by investors such as RAISE Ventures, Partech, Blackfin Capital Partners, Aglaé Ventures, Orange Ventures, and Portage. eurazeo::Ledger.notes: Ledger is a real company headquartered in Paris, France, specializing in hardware wallets and crypto security. It is a portfolio company of Eurazeo, having received investment from Idinvest Partners (which was acquired by Eurazeo and rebranded as Eurazeo Growth) during its Series B and Series C funding rounds. As of early 2026, Ledger remains a private company and is still listed as a portfolio asset in Eurazeo's growth strategy.

eurazeo::Dataiku.notes: Dataiku is a real technology company headquartered in New York. Eurazeo invested in Dataiku during its Series E funding round in 2021 and continues to list the company as an active 'In portfolio' investment on its official website as of early 2026.

eurazeo::360Learning.notes: 360Learning is a real EdTech company headquartered in Paris. It became a portfolio company of Eurazeo following Eurazeo's acquisition and merger with Idinvest Partners, which was an early investor in the company (e.g., Series A in 2015). As of early 2026, 360Learning remains a private company with no recorded exit by Eurazeo.

eurazeo::OpenClassrooms.notes: OpenClassrooms is a Paris-based online education platform. It became a portfolio company of Eurazeo following Eurazeo's acquisition of Idinvest Partners (now part of Eurazeo Growth), which led OpenClassrooms' $60 million Series B round in 2018. It is still listed as a portfolio company in recent investor reports and Eurazeo's own publications.

eurazeo::Meero.notes: Meero is a Paris-based technology company specializing in AI-driven photography. Eurazeo (via Eurazeo Growth) acquired a minority stake in Meero in June 2019 during its $230 million Series C round. As of Eurazeo's 2024 Universal Registration Document (filed in March 2025) and recent 2026 database records, Meero remains an active portfolio company.

eurazeo::GitGuardian.notes: GitGuardian is a Paris-based cybersecurity firm. Eurazeo led its $44M Series B round in December 2021 and participated as an existing investor in its $50M Series C round in February 2026, confirming its status as a current portfolio company.

eurazeo::Mistral AI.notes: Mistral AI is a Paris-based technology company. Eurazeo is confirmed as an investor, having participated in Mistral AI's $640 million (€600 million) Series B funding round in June 2024.

eurazeo::Sorare.notes: Sorare is a Paris-based fantasy sports and NFT platform. Eurazeo participated in its $680 million Series B funding round in September 2021 and continues to list it as a portfolio company in recent 2025 and 2026 reports.

eurazeo::Grab.notes: Grab is a Singapore-based super-app. Eurazeo invested in Grab in 2019 (via its Smart City fund) and officially recorded it as an exit following Grab's de-SPAC merger and public listing on the NASDAQ in December 2021.

eurazeo::Iberchem.notes: Iberchem is a fragrance and flavor manufacturer headquartered in Murcia, Spain. Eurazeo acquired a majority stake in the company in July 2017 and successfully exited the investment in November 2020 by selling it to the UK-based specialty chemicals group Croda International for €820 million.

eurazeo::Premium Group.notes: Eurazeo (via Eurazeo PME) acquired a majority stake in Groupe Premium in 2021. In July 2023, Blackstone invested €400m for a minority stake, but Eurazeo retained controlling interest and remains the lead investor.

eurazeo::Colisée.notes: Colisée is a French healthcare group specializing in nursing homes. Eurazeo (via its subsidiary Eurazeo PME) acquired the company in 2014 and successfully exited the investment in 2017 by selling it to IK Investment Partners.

capza::Questel.notes: Questel is a Paris-based IP software and services company. CAPZA (formerly Capzanine) was an equity shareholder from 2014 until 2018, when it sold its stake to IK Partners. While CAPZA has since provided debt financing (unitranche) for Questel, its status as an equity portfolio company is considered 'exited'.

capza::Ivnosys.notes: Ivnosys is a Spanish e-identity company headquartered in Valencia. CAPZA (formerly Capzanine) acquired a minority stake in January 2019 and exited in 2021 when it sold its stake to PSG, which merged Ivnosys with Signaturit.

capza::Horizon Software.notes: Horizon Software was acquired by CAPZA in 2018 and was a portfolio company until May 2022, when CAPZA sold its majority stake to Sagard NewGen.

capza::Nutripure.notes: Nutripure is a real company based near Toulouse, but it is not a portfolio company of CAPZA. It was previously held by Ardian and Bpifrance and was acquired by PAI Partners in July 2024. CAPZA is invested in a similar French food supplement company called Nutravalia.

capza::Recommerce.notes: Recommerce is a real company based in Gentilly, France, specializing in refurbished electronics.
